dedupe_keys.name: cell tower detection from maxar imagery using openstreetmap derived labels sub saharan africa

description: This paper demonstrates a partially automated workflow to train an object detection model that locates cell towers in high-resolution Maxar imagery, using OpenStreetMap features to generate annotations. It targets rural sub-Saharan Africa, where coverage and high-speed service gaps persist and better maps of telecommunications infrastructure can inform strategies to close them. The authors curated a dataset of over 6,000 unique tower images from 26 countries in eastern, southern and central Africa and report an average precision at 50 percent intersection over union of 81.2, with good performance across geographies and in out-of-sample tests; more accurate tower locations can yield more accurate cell coverage maps for decision support. Producer: Krell and co-authors, submitted to arXiv on 14 November 2023 (computer vision). Coverage: 26 African countries. Access: the paper on arXiv; the abstract page gives no link to the model or dataset. Licence and cost: not stated for the model code; the paper is free and CC BY 4.0. Caveats: Maxar imagery is commercial, OSM-derived labels may be incomplete, and towers of unusual design may be missed. Simulation uses: it produces tower inventories where none exist, feeding coverage, exposure and resilience analysis of mobile networks. Related record: OpenCellID (data-opencellid), a crowdsourced tower database usable for comparison.
